note: Which kit model stands in for each archetype, and where that model's paint
lives in the shared palette atlas.
Kenney's Car Kit puts every model on one material sampling one 512x512
palette texture, so a car is repainted by editing the texture rather than
by touching the model. Each model ships in its own colour, so there is no
single paint band -- the source hue is declared per model here.
The bands were measured area-weighted off each body mesh's UVs, not by
vertex count: a big flat roof is few vertices and a detailed bumper is
many, so counting vertices reports the bumper as the car's colour.
minSaturation is what separates paint from the shared chassis. Every model
carries a #66677c blue-grey underside at roughly 40% of its surface, which
sits inside the blue hue window but at a saturation of ~0.15. The van's
actual blue paint is ~0.53. That threshold is the only thing keeping a
repaint off the chassis, so do not lower it without re-checking a render.
KNOWN AND ACCEPTED: lamp lenses share a hue window with paint on the red
and amber models, so they repaint along with the bodywork. They are a
fraction of a percent of the surface and invisible at lot scale. Splitting
them out would mean editing UVs, which is a model change, not a texture one.
Declared in archetypes.ts but not produced by any model in the
catalogue, so nothing renders them. Left here so the reason is on the
record rather than looking like an oversight; if a premium hatch or a
plain two-door is ever added to models.ts, these need entries above and
the render matrix grows by nine frames each.
